correctness.rationale: The normalized Poisson kernel is integrated with measure dt/(2π), and the maximin upper bound is its symmetric average. Bathtub superlevel maximizers are reflection invariant, equalize both source measures, and thus attain the bound. The rational density derivative q(u) strictly decreases, giving a single angle mode threshold c*(r). Exact factorization of H(u)-H(1) yields u0=kc+c²−1 and critical occupied measure arccos(u0)/π; strict angular monotonicity of integrated Poisson density proves the best connected arc is the midpoint. A local Taylor expansion proves the square-root merger law. All degeneracies and ranges are described explicitly; symbolic polynomial checks and 953 deterministic corroborative numerical assertions were run, without treating finite tests as global proofs.

value.rationale: Harmonic measure is canonical for observing boundary events from prescribed interior points. The new claim settles a structurally meaningful two-point worst-case observation problem, including an exact geometric phase transition in the number of components, a quantitative critical boundary length, unique optimizer geometry and a strict price for connected sensing; these go beyond the known bathtub rule and describe an unknown exact natural design invariant. It is not merely an arbitrary numeric slice or an exercise in changing names. Restricted to equiradial pairs, with no unproved generalizations claimed.
